records.name: 1Zpresso J-Max
records.descSnippet: The 1Zpresso J-Max is a Taiwanese hand grinder with 48 mm coated burrs and fine external numbered adjustment, well suited to espresso and fine filter. See 1Zpresso J-Max.

records.name: Acaia Lunar
records.descSnippet: The Acaia Lunar is a compact, water-resistant espresso scale built to sit on the drip tray and track dose, yield, and time as the shot pulls. See Acaia Lunar.

records.name: Acaia Pearl
records.descSnippet: The Acaia Pearl is a fast, app-connected brewing scale with 0.1 gram resolution and flow-rate readouts, a reference scale for the pour-over bench. See Acaia Pearl.

records.name: courge poivrée
records.descSnippet: Small ribbed winter squash with sweet, mild flesh; usually halved and roasted.

records.name: acrylic resolene finish
records.descSnippet: A thin acrylic topcoat that seals dye and adds a wipe-clean, water-resistant film over the surface.

records.name: AeroPress
records.descSnippet: The AeroPress steeps grounds in its chamber, then presses the brew through a paper cap by hand. Quick, near-unbreakable, and endlessly tweakable, it is a travel and daily staple. See AeroPress.

records.name: AeroPress brew
records.descSnippet: A quick immersion press: steep dosed, ground coffee in the chamber, then press it through a paper cap into the cup. Tolerant of grind error and easy to repeat.

records.name: AeroPress Paper Filter
records.descSnippet: AeroPress paper micro-filters are the small round filters that drop into the brewer's cap for a clean, sediment-free press. See AeroPress Paper Filter.

records.name: air still
records.descSnippet: A compact electric all-in-one still that heats, distills, and air-cools in a single benchtop unit. Small in capacity and easy to run, it is a common entry point for hobby distilling and for making…

records.name: ale yeast
records.descSnippet: A brewer's top-fermenting yeast that brings fruity, estery flavors. Borrowed from beer making, it suits a grain wash where some of that character should carry into the spirit.

records.name: pomme
records.descSnippet: Crisp, sweet-tart pome fruit; eaten fresh, baked, juiced, or fermented to cider.

records.name: abricot
records.descSnippet: Small orange drupe, sweet-tart; eaten fresh, dried, or in jams and bakes.

records.name: artichaut
records.descSnippet: Edible flower bud; the fleshy leaf bases and heart are eaten cooked.

records.name: roquette
records.descSnippet: Peppery salad leaf; eaten raw or wilted onto warm dishes.

records.name: asperge
records.descSnippet: Tender young spear, green or white; steamed, roasted, or grilled.

records.name: avocat
records.descSnippet: Rich, buttery-fleshed fruit with a large stone; eaten as a savoury vegetable.

records.name: backflushing
records.descSnippet: Clean an espresso machine's group by running water back through a blind basket with detergent, clearing oils that would otherwise turn the next shots bitter.

records.name: banane
records.descSnippet: Soft, sweet, energy-dense tropical fruit in a peelable skin; eaten fresh or baked.

records.name: Baratza Encore
records.descSnippet: The Baratza Encore is a widely recommended entry electric burr grinder for filter coffee, designed in Seattle and serviceable with available parts. See Baratza Encore.

records.name: Barry King maul
records.descSnippet: A Barry King tapered poly-head maul with a leather-wrapped handle and balanced steel/brass core — a widely cited bench-standard striking tool.

records.name: beeswax
records.descSnippet: Natural wax for waxing bare thread and slicking edges; also a simple burnishing aid.

records.name: betterave
records.descSnippet: Earthy, sweet deep-red taproot; roasted, boiled, pickled, or grated raw.

records.name: poivron
records.descSnippet: Sweet, crisp, hollow capsicum in green/red/yellow; raw, roasted, or stuffed.

records.name: Bialetti Moka Express
records.descSnippet: Bialetti's Moka Express is the original aluminum stovetop moka pot, an Italian icon since the 1930s, pushing steam-pressured water through the grounds for a strong, concentrated brew. See Bialetti…

records.name: mûre
records.descSnippet: Dark, glossy aggregate berry, sweet with a tart edge; grows on brambles.

records.name: cassis
records.descSnippet: Intensely aromatic dark berry, tart and musky; base of cordials, jams and liqueurs.

records.name: blade grinder
records.descSnippet: A spinning-blade chopper that cuts beans unevenly into a mix of dust and chunks. Cheap and common, but it cannot grind evenly, so a burr grinder is preferred for any careful brew.

records.name: blooming
records.descSnippet: Wet the dry grounds with a small first pour and wait, letting trapped gas escape so the following pours extract evenly. A short bloom of about 30 to 45 seconds is typical.

records.name: myrtille
records.descSnippet: Small blue-purple berry, sweet-tart; eaten fresh, baked, or in jams.

records.name: Bodum Chambord
records.descSnippet: Bodum's Chambord is the classic French press shape, a borosilicate beaker in a chrome frame with a mesh plunger, made in Portugal. A full-immersion standard for full-bodied coffee. See Bodum Chambord.

records.name: bok choy
records.descSnippet: Chinese cabbage with crisp white stalks and tender green leaves; stir-fried or in soups.

records.name: bone folder
records.descSnippet: A smooth blade for creasing folds, pressing seams, and working leather without leaving tool marks.

records.name: botanical grinder
records.descSnippet: A grinder that cracks or coarsely mills seeds, roots, and dried botanicals to open up their surface before they are macerated or loaded into a basket, releasing more aroma into the spirit.

records.name: Breville Bambino Plus
records.descSnippet: Breville's Bambino Plus is a compact home espresso machine with a fast thermojet heater and automatic milk steaming, a popular entry into the category. Sold as Sage in the UK and EU. See Breville…

records.name: brew ratio selection
records.descSnippet: Choose the ratio of coffee to water, often written like 1:16, that sets the strength of the cup. Lock the ratio first, then adjust grind and time to taste.

records.name: brew scale
records.descSnippet: A 0.1 gram scale with a timer, used to weigh the dose and the water and to track the pour in real time. Weighing rather than scooping is where repeatable brewing starts.

records.name: brew timer
records.descSnippet: A timer started with the pour so every phase, bloom, steep, and total brew time, is recorded against the result.

records.name: brew water
records.descSnippet: The water that makes up almost all of the cup. Its mineral content and temperature shape extraction and flavor as much as the beans do.

records.name: brewery wash
records.descSnippet: An alkaline cleaning powder that lifts wash residue and oils from fermenters and still parts without scrubbing, rinsing away clean.

records.name: Brewing America Proof and Tralle Hydrometer
records.descSnippet: Brewing America's proof-and-tralle hydrometer reads US proof and percent alcohol on the clear distillate, a traceable, US-made instrument for setting a spirit's strength. See Brewing America Proof &…

records.name: bridle leather
records.descSnippet: Firm veg-tan stuffed with oils and waxes on both faces — smooth, durable, and a classic for belts, straps and wallets.

records.name: brocoli
records.descSnippet: Green flowering brassica eaten as florets and stalk; steamed, roasted, or stir-fried.

records.name: chou de Bruxelles
records.descSnippet: Small cabbage-like buds on a stalk; roasted, sautéed, or shredded raw.

records.name: buckle
records.descSnippet: A framed fastener with a tongue for adjustable straps on belts, bags and gear.

records.name: courge butternut
records.descSnippet: Sweet, nutty winter squash with dense orange flesh; roasted or in soups.

records.name: button stud
records.descSnippet: A post-and-disc stud that a slotted strap or keeper slips over — a tidy closure for wallets and cases.

records.name: chou
records.descSnippet: Dense leafy head; eaten raw (slaw), braised, fermented (sauerkraut, kimchi).

records.name: CAFEC Abaca Filter
records.descSnippet: CAFEC's Abaca filter, made in Japan by Sanyo Sangyo, is a fast-draining paper made with manila hemp fiber, known for a clean cup and quick flow. See CAFEC Abaca Filter.

records.name: cane sugar
records.descSnippet: Refined sugar that dissolves straight into water for a clean, simple wash. It needs no mashing and ferments fast, the usual base for a neutral sugar-wash spirit.

records.name: cantaloup
records.descSnippet: Aromatic muskmelon with netted rind and sweet orange flesh.

records.name: carafe brewer
records.descSnippet: A one-piece glass brewer where a cone sits over a carafe, so the brew collects in the vessel you serve from. A thick paper filter gives a very clean, bright cup.

records.name: carboy
records.descSnippet: A narrow-necked glass or plastic jug used to ferment and age under an airlock. Its small surface at the top limits the wash's contact with air, which suits longer fermentations like wine and mead.

records.name: card holder
records.descSnippet: A slim two- or three-pocket holder, saddle-stitched at the sides with burnished edges — a step up in stitching and edge work. This is an exemplary template, not a fixed pattern — adapt the pieces,…

records.name: carotte
records.descSnippet: Sweet, crunchy orange taproot; eaten raw, cooked, or juiced.

records.name: Carter-head still
records.descSnippet: A still whose vapor passes up through a chamber of botanicals held in the head before it reaches the condenser. It is the classic vapor-infusion architecture for delicate gins, lifting aromatics…

records.name: chou-fleur
records.descSnippet: Dense white flowering head; roasted, mashed, riced, or in gratins.

records.name: céleri-rave
records.descSnippet: Knobbly celery-flavoured root; remoulade, purée, roasted, or in soups.

records.name: céleri
records.descSnippet: Crisp, fibrous, aromatic stalk; eaten raw or as an aromatic base (mirepoix/soffritto).

records.name: charred oak
records.descSnippet: Oak whose surface has been burned to a layer of char. The char filters harsher notes and releases vanilla and caramel flavors, the inside of a bourbon barrel in chip or stave form.

records.name: Chemex brew
records.descSnippet: A carafe pour-over through a thick bonded filter for a very clean, bright cup: bloom, then pour continuously to the target weight.

records.name: Chemex Classic
records.descSnippet: The Chemex is a one-piece hourglass carafe that brews through its own thick bonded paper filter, giving an exceptionally clean, bright cup. A mid-century design made in Massachusetts. See Chemex…

records.name: cerise
records.descSnippet: Small round drupe on a long stem, sweet or sour; eaten fresh, baked, or preserved.

records.name: chicago screw
records.descSnippet: A screw-together post and cap that fastens layers but can be opened again — ideal where parts may need swapping.

records.name: pois chiche
records.descSnippet: Nutty, firm pulse usually sold dried or cooked; base of hummus, stews and curries.

records.name: piment
records.descSnippet: Hot capsicum used fresh or dried to add pungent heat.

records.name: chisel-punching stitch holes
records.descSnippet: Drive a diamond chisel through the leather along the marked line to cut evenly spaced, angled stitch slits.

records.name: ciboulette
records.descSnippet: Slender, mildly oniony herb-allium; snipped raw as a garnish.

records.name: chrome-tanned leather
records.descSnippet: Soft, pliable hide tanned with chromium salts; common for garments, linings and bags, and the most forgiving to stitch.

records.name: citric acid
records.descSnippet: A mild acid used to clean and brighten copper and to strip light scale from still parts between runs.

records.name: citrus peel
records.descSnippet: Dried lemon, orange, or grapefruit peel that brings bright citrus oils to a gin or a distilled aromatic. The pith is left off to avoid bitterness.

records.name: clémentine
records.descSnippet: Seedless mandarin hybrid; sweet, juicy and easy to peel, popular in winter.

records.name: Clever Coffee Dripper
records.descSnippet: The Clever Dripper, made by ABID Co. in Taiwan, holds the brew with a base valve that opens only when you set it on a cup. Full immersion with a clean paper-filtered finish, and very easy to repeat.…

records.name: cloth filter
records.descSnippet: A reusable cloth filter that gives a clean cup with a softer body than paper; it must be rinsed and stored with care to stay fresh.

records.name: noix de coco
records.descSnippet: Large tropical drupe yielding firm white flesh, water and milk.

records.name: coffee blend
records.descSnippet: Coffee combining beans from several origins or roasts for a consistent, designed flavor that holds up year-round.

records.name: cold brew
records.descSnippet: A cold-brew run: steep time, grind, and dilution bind per batch, and the run records the concentrate it yields.

records.name: cold brew maker
records.descSnippet: A vessel that steeps coarse grounds in cold or room-temperature water for many hours, then filters them out, yielding a smooth, low-acid concentrate.

records.name: cold brew steep
records.descSnippet: A long cold steep for a smooth, low-acid concentrate: combine coarse grounds and cold water, steep for many hours, then filter out the grounds.

records.name: column packing
records.descSnippet: Material loaded into a reflux column to create surface for vapor and liquid to meet, from copper mesh that also scrubs sulfur to ceramic rings or stainless structured packing. More surface means more…

records.name: Comandante C40 MK4
records.descSnippet: The Comandante C40 MK4 is a German-made hand grinder whose hardened steel Nitro Blade burrs set a quality reference for manual grinding across filter and press. See Comandante C40 MK4.

records.name: conical fermenter
records.descSnippet: A tank with a cone-shaped bottom so spent yeast and solids settle into the tip and can be drawn off, leaving cleaner wash above. The shape makes it easy to harvest sediment between batches.

records.name: contact cement
records.descSnippet: A water-based contact adhesive applied to both faces and bonded under pressure to hold pieces aligned for stitching.

records.name: continuous pouring
records.descSnippet: Pour in one steady spiral from center out, holding a constant flow and level. Simple and forgiving on larger brewers.

records.name: copper alembic
records.descSnippet: A traditional onion-shaped copper pot with a swan neck and a coil condenser. The copper reacts with sulfur compounds to clean the spirit, and the same form serves spirits, essential oils, and…

records.name: CopperHolic Copper Alembic
records.descSnippet: CopperHolic sells hand-hammered copper alembic still kits for essential oils, hydrosols, and distilled water, in several sizes for hobby and small-batch use. See CopperHolic.

records.name: coriander seed
records.descSnippet: A warm, citrusy, slightly spicy seed that is gin's usual second botanical after juniper, lifting and rounding the aroma.

records.name: canneberge
records.descSnippet: Firm, very tart red berry, usually cooked or dried with sugar; classic with poultry.

records.name: concombre
records.descSnippet: Cool, crisp, watery cucurbit eaten raw or pickled.

records.name: culinary herb
records.descSnippet: A fresh or dried kitchen herb such as rosemary, thyme, or mint, distilled for its aromatic oil and water or used to flavor a spirit.

records.name: cupping bowl
records.descSnippet: A standard wide bowl used to taste several coffees side by side under the same conditions, the shared vessel of the tasting table.

records.name: cut pieces from pattern
records.descSnippet: Lay out a pattern and cut clean, accurate pieces — the start of every project.

records.name: self-healing cutting mat
records.descSnippet: A gridded, self-closing work surface that takes the blade without dulling it or scarring the bench.

records.name: cutting to pattern
records.descSnippet: Trace a pattern onto the leather and cut the pieces cleanly against a straightedge on a protected surface.

records.name: D-ring
records.descSnippet: A D-shaped ring anchored to leather as an attachment point for straps, snap hooks and hardware.

records.name: dark roast coffee
records.descSnippet: Coffee roasted long and deep, with bittersweet, roasty flavors and a heavier body. Lower in perceived acidity, usually brewed a little cooler.

records.name: datte
records.descSnippet: Very sweet, chewy fruit of the date palm, usually eaten dried; a natural sweetener.

records.name: decaffeinated coffee
records.descSnippet: Coffee with most of its caffeine removed before roasting, brewed the same as any other coffee.

records.name: demijohn
records.descSnippet: A large bulbous bottle, often in a basket, used to ferment or hold a batch of wash or wine. It works much like a carboy at a larger volume.

records.name: dephlegmator
records.descSnippet: A partial condenser at the top of a column that knocks some vapor back down as liquid. By adjusting its cooling water the operator dials how much reflux the column runs, trading flavor for purity in…

records.name: descaler
records.descSnippet: A mild acid solution that dissolves limescale from a kettle or an espresso machine's boiler and lines to keep heating and flow steady.

records.name: descaling
records.descSnippet: Flush a kettle or machine with a mild acid solution to dissolve limescale from the boiler and lines, keeping heating and flow steady.

records.name: diamond stitching chisel
records.descSnippet: A multi-prong chisel driven through the leather to cut evenly spaced, angled slits for saddle stitching.

records.name: DiFluid R2 Extract
records.descSnippet: The DiFluid R2 Extract is a compact, affordable digital refractometer that brought TDS measurement within reach of home baristas. See DiFluid R2 Extract.

records.name: distilled water
records.descSnippet: Water with its minerals removed. Flat on its own for brewing, it is the blank base for a remineralized recipe.

records.name: distillers yeast
records.descSnippet: A yeast strain selected for spirit washes, fermenting cleanly and tolerating a fair amount of alcohol. It gives a neutral-to-characterful base depending on the strain.

records.name: distribution tool
records.descSnippet: A spinning leveling tool that smooths the surface of the grounds to an even depth before tamping.

records.name: dosing and weighing
records.descSnippet: Weigh the beans before grinding so every brew starts from the same dose. Weighing rather than scooping is the first step to a result you can repeat and compare.

records.name: dosing funnel
records.descSnippet: A ring or funnel that sits on the portafilter to guide grounds in without spilling, keeping the dose and the bench clean.

records.name: double-cap rivet
records.descSnippet: A rivet finished on both faces, so the join looks clean from either side — common on straps and small goods.

records.name: fruit du dragon
records.descSnippet: Striking cactus fruit with vivid skin and mild, sweet, seed-flecked flesh.

records.name: drawstring pouch
records.descSnippet: A round-bottomed pouch closed by a cord threaded through eyelets — mostly cutting and punching, a gentle introduction to bag shapes. This is an exemplary template, not a fixed pattern — adapt the…

records.name: edamame
records.descSnippet: Young green soybeans, boiled or steamed in the pod; nutty and protein-rich.

records.name: edge beveler
records.descSnippet: A grooved blade that shaves the square corner off an edge, rounding it so it burnishes smooth.

records.name: edge beveling
records.descSnippet: Trim the square corner off a cut edge so it rounds over and takes a clean burnish.

records.name: edge burnishing
records.descSnippet: Lay the edge fibers down and polish them to a hard sheen by working a slicker over a dampened, gummed edge with friction.

records.name: edge burnishing gum
records.descSnippet: A gum-and-wax compound worked into an edge before slicking to lay the fibers down and bring up a hard, glassy finish.

records.name: edge creaser
records.descSnippet: Presses a fine decorative bead line parallel to an edge or pocket top for a finished, framed look.

records.name: edge creasing
records.descSnippet: Press a fine bead line parallel to an edge or pocket top for a finished, framed look.

records.name: edge dyeing
records.descSnippet: Apply dye to a beveled edge before burnishing to frame the piece with a crisp line of color.

records.name: edge planer
records.descSnippet: Shaves a stacked, glued edge flat and even so the layers read as one before finishing.

records.name: edge slicker
records.descSnippet: A grooved wood or poly tool rubbed along a dampened edge to friction-polish the fibers to a hard sheen.

records.name: aubergine
records.descSnippet: Spongy-fleshed nightshade fruit; grilled, roasted, fried, or stewed.

records.name: electric element with controller
records.descSnippet: An electric heating element in the pot paired with a power controller. Setting the wattage gives steady, repeatable heat and a controllable vapor speed, which is why it is the common choice for…

records.name: electric grinder
records.descSnippet: A motorized burr grinder for the home bench, grinding a dose at the press of a button with repeatable settings across filter and press brewing.

records.name: endive
records.descSnippet: Slightly bitter salad leaf; eaten raw or braised.

records.name: espresso brew
records.descSnippet: An espresso brew run: dose, distribution, and tamp are protocol, while grind setting and yield bind per shot. The run captures dose in, yield out, time, and taste.

records.name: espresso dosing and distribution
records.descSnippet: Dose the ground coffee into the basket, then break up clumps and level the bed with a needle tool so water meets even resistance. The foundation of an even shot.

records.name: espresso grinder
records.descSnippet: A burr grinder built for the fine, precise grind espresso needs, with small-step or stepless adjustment so you can dial a shot in tenths of a setting.

records.name: espresso machine
records.descSnippet: A machine that forces hot water through a compacted puck of finely ground coffee at around nine bars, pulling a small, intense shot topped with crema.

records.name: espresso machine cleaner
records.descSnippet: A detergent powder or tablet used to backflush an espresso machine and clean baskets and portafilters of coffee oils.

records.name: espresso roast coffee
records.descSnippet: Coffee roasted and blended to taste well as espresso: enough development for body and sweetness under pressure, often with a comfortable grind window.

records.name: espresso scale
records.descSnippet: A small, fast scale that fits on the drip tray to weigh the shot as it pulls, tracking dose in, yield out, and shot time together.

records.name: espresso shot pull
records.descSnippet: Pull a shot of espresso: dose and distribute, tamp level, then run the pump and dial grind to land the shot in its target ratio and time.

records.name: eyelet
records.descSnippet: A metal ring set into a punched hole to reinforce it for lacing, cord or drawstrings.

records.name: fève
records.descSnippet: Large flat green bean in a thick pod; shelled and often double-podded before cooking.

records.name: Fellow Ode Gen 2
records.descSnippet: The Fellow Ode Gen 2 is a single-dose electric brew grinder with 64 mm flat burrs, tuned for filter methods and a quiet, low-retention workflow. See Fellow Ode Gen 2.

records.name: Fellow Stagg EKG
records.descSnippet: Fellow's Stagg EKG is a variable-temperature electric gooseneck kettle with a precise spout and a set-and-hold readout, a fixture of the pour-over bench. See Fellow Stagg EKG.

records.name: fenouil
records.descSnippet: Crisp anise-flavoured bulb; eaten raw shaved or braised and roasted.

records.name: fermenter
records.descSnippet: A food-grade vessel where yeast turns sugars into alcohol. It holds the wash under an airlock that lets carbon dioxide out while keeping air and contaminants from getting in.

records.name: Fiebing's Pro Dye
records.descSnippet: Fiebing's Pro Dye — a penetrating oil-based leather dye, a long-standing North-American reference for even, colorfast coverage on veg-tan.

records.name: figue
records.descSnippet: Soft, sweet fruit with seedy flesh; eaten fresh or dried, sweet and savoury.

records.name: filtered water
records.descSnippet: Tap water passed through a filter to cut chlorine and some hardness, a clean and practical base for brewing.

records.name: finish an edge
records.descSnippet: Take a raw cut edge to a smooth, sealed finish: bevel the corners, sand it true, then burnish it hard.

records.name: Flair 58
records.descSnippet: The Flair 58 is a manual lever espresso maker with a 58 mm portafilter and a heated group, so you pull real espresso by hand with full control of the pressure. Made by Flair Espresso. See Flair 58.

records.name: flaked corn
records.descSnippet: Corn in a form that gels and releases its starch in the mash. It ferments to a soft, sweet spirit and is the dominant grain in bourbon-style whiskey.

records.name: flat-bottom dripper
records.descSnippet: A flat-bottomed dripper with a few small holes that spreads the grounds in an even bed, giving a forgiving, repeatable extraction that is easy to dial in.

records.name: Florentine flask
records.descSnippet: A vessel fed by the condenser that lets a distillation's oil and water settle and part. The essential oil, usually the lighter layer, floats off while the aromatic water, the hydrosol, is drawn from…

records.name: French press
records.descSnippet: A tall beaker with a mesh plunger. Grounds steep fully in the water, then the plunger traps them at the bottom for a heavy, full-bodied cup with some sediment.

records.name: French press immersion brew
records.descSnippet: A full-immersion press for a heavy, full-bodied cup: steep coarse grounds, then plunge to separate them from the brew.

records.name: fruit mash
records.descSnippet: Crushed ripe fruit whose natural sugars ferment on their own or with added yeast. The fermented fruit is distilled into brandy or eau de vie.

records.name: Gaggia Classic Pro
records.descSnippet: The Gaggia Classic Pro is a long-running Italian home machine with a commercial-style portafilter and a simple, repairable design that makes it a favorite first manual espresso machine. See Gaggia…

records.name: ail
records.descSnippet: Intensely aromatic bulb of cloves; a near-universal savoury seasoning.

records.name: gas burner
records.descSnippet: An open gas flame under the still pot. Powerful and cheap, it heats fast but is harder to hold steady, so many operators move to electric for the slow, even heat a careful spirit run wants.

records.name: gin basket
records.descSnippet: A perforated basket that holds botanicals in the vapor path above the wash. Alcohol vapor rising through it picks up the lighter, brighter aromatics, the vapor-infusion route to a delicate gin.

records.name: gingembre
records.descSnippet: Pungent, warming rhizome used fresh or dried to season sweet and savoury dishes.

records.name: glass aging vessel
records.descSnippet: A glass jar or bottle aged with oak chips, staves, or spirals inside. It mimics barrel character at small scale and lets the maker taste the wood's effect over time without committing a whole cask.

records.name: glue and stitch a lap seam
records.descSnippet: Cement two layers together for alignment, then saddle-stitch through the bonded lap for strength.

records.name: groseille à maquereau
records.descSnippet: Tart, translucent berry on a thorny bush; cooked into pies, fools and preserves.

records.name: gooseneck kettle
records.descSnippet: A kettle with a long, narrow swan-neck spout that gives a slow, precise, steerable stream, the standard for controlled pour-over.

records.name: raisin
records.descSnippet: Juicy vine fruit borne in clusters; eaten fresh, dried (raisin), or pressed for wine.

records.name: grape must
records.descSnippet: Freshly pressed grape juice with its skins and pulp. Fermented to wine and then distilled, it is the starting point for grape brandy and pomace spirits.

records.name: pamplemousse
records.descSnippet: Large citrus with bittersweet, slightly sour flesh; eaten fresh or juiced.

records.name: haricot vert
records.descSnippet: Tender immature bean pod eaten whole; steamed, sautéed, or blanched.

records.name: grind size selection
records.descSnippet: Pick a grind size to match the method: coarse for press and cold brew, medium for drip, fine for espresso. Finer grinds extract faster, so grind is the main lever you turn when a brew tastes weak or…

records.name: grinder cleaning
records.descSnippet: Brush out and wipe down the burrs and chamber so stale grounds and oils do not taint fresh coffee or clog the path.

records.name: goyave
records.descSnippet: Fragrant tropical fruit with sweet pink or white flesh; eaten fresh or as paste/juice.

records.name: gum tragacanth
records.descSnippet: A traditional plant-gum edge slicking agent — brushed on, then burnished to seal and smooth the edge.

records.name: hand grinder
records.descSnippet: A manual burr grinder: you turn a handle to crush beans between two burrs at a set gap. Quiet, portable, and capable of an even grind for any brew method.

records.name: hand press
records.descSnippet: A bench press that sets hardware, punches, and stamps with steady leverage instead of repeated blows.

records.name: Hario V60 Buono Kettle
records.descSnippet: Hario's V60 Buono is a stovetop gooseneck kettle whose narrow spout gives the slow, steerable stream pour-over needs. See Hario V60 Buono Kettle.

records.name: Hario V60 Drip Scale
records.descSnippet: Hario's V60 Drip Scale is a simple brewing scale and timer sized for single-cup pour-over, weighing dose and water on one display. See Hario V60 Drip Scale.

records.name: Hario Switch
records.descSnippet: Hario's Switch pairs a V60-style cone with a stainless ball valve in the base, so you can steep like immersion and then release through paper. One brewer, two methods. See Hario Switch.

records.name: Hario V60
records.descSnippet: Hario's V60 is the archetypal cone dripper, with a 60-degree wall, one large opening, and tall spiral ribs that let your pour drive the extraction. A reference point for specialty pour-over…

records.name: Hario V60 Paper Filter
records.descSnippet: Hario's V60 paper filters are the cone filters cut to fit the V60's spiral-ribbed wall, sized 01, 02, and 03 to the brewer. See Hario V60 Paper Filter.

records.name: harness leather
records.descSnippet: Tough, weather-resistant veg-tan with lower oil content, built for straps and gear that take real load and exposure.

records.name: harness needle
records.descSnippet: A blunt, large-eye needle that passes through pre-made holes without snagging the thread or your fingers.

records.name: head knife
records.descSnippet: A half-moon blade for straight cuts, curves, skiving and paring — the traditional all-rounder of the bench.

records.name: Hillbilly Flute
records.descSnippet: Hillbilly Stills' Flute is a plated reflux column you can run at different plate counts for anything from flavorful whiskey to near-neutral spirit, a popular US-made modular still. See Hillbilly…

records.name: hole punch
records.descSnippet: A single-size tube driven with a mallet to punch one hole — sized to the rivet, snap or lace it serves.

records.name: honey
records.descSnippet: Diluted in water and fermented, honey makes mead, and a fermented honey wash can be distilled into a honey spirit. Its sugars are fully fermentable.

records.name: melon miel
records.descSnippet: Smooth-skinned melon with sweet, pale green flesh.

records.name: HOOLOO 8 L Essential Oil Still
records.descSnippet: HOOLOO's 8 L copper still is built for essential oils and hydrosols, passing steam through a botanical chamber and parting the oil and water at a separator. See HOOLOO Essential Oil Still.

records.name: raifort
records.descSnippet: Fiercely pungent root, grated as a condiment; sharp, sinus-clearing heat.

records.name: hybrid still
records.descSnippet: A still that can run as a pot or as a column, usually by switching a valve or bypassing the plates. One vessel covers flavorful spirit runs and high-proof neutral runs, which is why small…

records.name: hydrometer
records.descSnippet: A weighted float that sits lower in lighter liquid, read against a scale. A spirit hydrometer or alcoholmeter reads alcohol by volume directly, the basic instrument for telling how strong a…

records.name: Iberian Coppers Essential Oil Alembic
records.descSnippet: Iberian Coppers, of Portugal, hand-hammers copper alembic still kits for essential oils, hydrosols, distilled water, and spirits, in a long alembic-making tradition. See Iberian Coppers.

records.name: immersion brew
records.descSnippet: An immersion brew run, such as a French press: steep time and grind bind per brew, and the run records the cup against them.

records.name: immersion press
records.descSnippet: A piston-style brewer: grounds steep in the chamber, then you press the slurry through a filter cap by hand. Fast, portable, and tolerant of grind error.

records.name: immersion steeping
records.descSnippet: Let the grounds sit fully submerged for a set time so extraction is driven by contact, not pour. Forgiving and very repeatable.

records.name: iStill Mini
records.descSnippet: The iStill Mini is a fully automated hybrid still that runs software-driven recipes managing heat, reflux, and cuts. It works as both a pot and a column still and is aimed at serious hobby and small…

records.name: Joseph Flach & Sons Gin Botanicals
records.descSnippet: Joseph Flach & Sons, a long-established London spice house, supplies distillers' gin botanicals such as juniper, coriander, and angelica by the grade and lot. See Joseph Flach & Sons.

records.name: juniper berries
records.descSnippet: The piney, resinous berries that define gin. Macerated in the wash or held in a vapor basket, they are the one botanical a spirit must lead with to be called gin.

records.name: chou frisé
records.descSnippet: Hardy, robust brassica leaf; eaten raw massaged, sautéed, or in soups.

records.name: Kalita flat-bottom brew
records.descSnippet: A flat-bottom drip whose even bed forgives small errors: dose, grind, bloom, then pour in steady pulses to the target weight.

records.name: Kalita Wave 185
records.descSnippet: Kalita's Wave is a flat-bottom dripper with three small holes and a wavy paper filter that keeps the bed even and forgiving, prized for repeatable results. The 185 is the larger, multi-cup size. See…

records.name: key fob
records.descSnippet: A short strap folded around a split ring and riveted closed — the classic first project: one cut, a punch, a rivet, and finished edges. This is an exemplary template, not a fixed pattern — adapt the…

records.name: kiwi
records.descSnippet: Brown fuzzy-skinned fruit with bright green, tart-sweet flesh and tiny black seeds.

records.name: knock box
records.descSnippet: A box with a padded bar to knock the spent puck out of the portafilter between shots.

records.name: chou-rave
records.descSnippet: Crisp, mild swollen stem of a brassica; eaten raw or cooked.

records.name: kumquat
records.descSnippet: Tiny oval citrus eaten whole, skin and all; sweet rind around tart flesh.

records.name: La Marzocco Linea Mini
records.descSnippet: The Linea Mini brings La Marzocco's dual-boiler commercial engineering into a home machine, with the saturated group and temperature stability of its cafe lineage. See La Marzocco Linea Mini.

records.name: lavender
records.descSnippet: Fragrant lavender flowers, distilled with steam for their essential oil and floral hydrosol and used in small amounts as a gin botanical.

records.name: leather cementing
records.descSnippet: Coat both mating faces with contact cement, let them tack, then press together to hold the pieces aligned before stitching.

records.name: leather conditioner
records.descSnippet: A blend of oils and waxes that keeps finished leather supple and guards against drying and cracking.

records.name: leather dye
records.descSnippet: Penetrating color for leather and edges, applied by dauber, brush or airbrush before sealing and finishing.

records.name: leather scissors
records.descSnippet: Heavy shears for trimming thread and cutting thinner leathers and linings.

records.name: leather strap construction
records.descSnippet: Cut a strap, mark and punch the stitch line, saddle-stitch it, and finish the edges — the foundational small-goods procedure.

records.name: poireau
records.descSnippet: Mild, sweet allium with a long white stalk; the base of soups and braises.

records.name: citron
records.descSnippet: Tart yellow citrus; its juice and zest brighten sauces, dressings, bakes and drinks.

records.name: lentille
records.descSnippet: Small quick-cooking pulse in many colours; the heart of dals, soups and stews.

records.name: laitue
records.descSnippet: Crisp salad leaf in many forms; eaten raw as the base of salads.

records.name: Liebig condenser
records.descSnippet: A straight inner tube carrying vapor inside an outer water jacket. Cold water flows counter to the vapor and cools it back to liquid. Simple and reliable, it is the default condenser on many small…

records.name: light roast coffee
records.descSnippet: Coffee roasted lightly, stopping near or just after first crack. Bright and acidic with origin character to the fore, usually brewed with hotter water.

records.name: citron vert
records.descSnippet: Small green citrus, sharper and more aromatic than lemon; staple of Latin and Southeast Asian cooking.

records.name: litchi
records.descSnippet: Small tropical fruit with a rough red shell and sweet, floral translucent flesh.

records.name: lyne arm
records.descSnippet: The sloping tube that carries vapor from the top of the still to the condenser. Its angle and length influence reflux and so the weight of the spirit: an upward arm gives a lighter cut, a downward…

records.name: magnetic snap
records.descSnippet: A pair of magnetic discs set into the leather for a quiet, low-profile bag or flap closure.

records.name: mallet
records.descSnippet: A non-marring poly, rawhide or wooden head for driving chisels and punches and setting hardware — never steel-faced.

records.name: malted barley
records.descSnippet: Barley that has been germinated and kilned so its starches and the enzymes to convert them are ready. Mashed with hot water it gives a fermentable, malty wash, the base of malt whisky.

records.name: mandarine
records.descSnippet: Small, sweet, easy-peeling citrus with loose skin and segmented flesh.

records.name: mangue
records.descSnippet: Fragrant tropical drupe with sweet, juicy orange flesh around a flat stone.

records.name: manual lever espresso maker
records.descSnippet: A hand-powered espresso maker where you generate the brew pressure yourself with a lever or piston, trading convenience for full control of the pressure profile.

records.name: marking a stitch line
records.descSnippet: Scribe a guideline a set distance in from the edge so the stitch holes run straight and even.

records.name: maul
records.descSnippet: A weighted, tapered poly head that delivers a controlled, rolling strike — the bench upgrade from a flat mallet.

records.name: medium roast coffee
records.descSnippet: Coffee roasted to a balanced mid point, rounding origin character with some developed sweetness. The forgiving everyday choice across most methods.

records.name: mesh bag
records.descSnippet: A fine cloth or mesh bag that holds botanicals or grains in the liquid so they can steep and then be lifted out cleanly, keeping loose solids out of the wash or the still.

records.name: metal mesh filter
records.descSnippet: A reusable fine metal mesh that lets oils and fine particles through for a fuller, heavier body and no paper waste.

records.name: Midwest Barrel Co. Small-Format Cask
records.descSnippet: Midwest Barrel Co. supplies small-format charred oak barrels, from a liter up to a few liters, that mature spirit quickly for their size thanks to the high wood-to-spirit ratio. See Midwest Barrel…

records.name: milk drink
records.descSnippet: A milk espresso drink run: the espresso and the steamed milk combine into a latte or cappuccino, with the shot and milk texture recorded per drink.

records.name: milk drink build
records.descSnippet: Build a milk espresso drink: pull a shot, steam milk to glossy microfoam, and combine them into a latte or cappuccino.

records.name: milk pitcher
records.descSnippet: A spouted steel jug for steaming and pouring milk, sized to the drink and shaped to help form and control microfoam.

records.name: milk steaming and frothing
records.descSnippet: Steam milk with the wand to stretch and texture it into glossy microfoam, then swirl it smooth for pouring into espresso drinks.

records.name: mink oil
records.descSnippet: A softening, water-repelling dressing for conditioning and weatherproofing finished leather.

records.name: moka pot
records.descSnippet: A stovetop pot that pushes water up through a basket of grounds under steam pressure, producing a strong, concentrated coffee between drip and espresso.

records.name: moka pot brew
records.descSnippet: A stovetop moka brew: fill the base, load the basket, and heat until steam pressure pushes a strong, concentrated coffee up into the top.

records.name: molasses
records.descSnippet: The thick, dark syrup left from refining sugar cane. Rich in residual sugar and flavor, it ferments to the wash that is distilled into rum.

records.name: mug
records.descSnippet: The cup the coffee lands in or is served in. For single-cup brewing the dripper often sits straight on the mug.

records.name: neatsfoot oil
records.descSnippet: A conditioning oil that restores suppleness and deepens color in veg-tan; applied sparingly to avoid over-softening.

records.name: nectarine
records.descSnippet: Smooth-skinned variety of peach, firm and sweet, with a single stone.

records.name: Niche Zero
records.descSnippet: The Niche Zero is a UK-made single-dose grinder with a 63 mm conical burr and near-zero retention, popular for moving cleanly between espresso and filter. See Niche Zero.

records.name: North Mountain Supply Alcoholmeter
records.descSnippet: North Mountain Supply's glass alcoholmeter carries proof and Tralle scales for reading the strength of a finished distillate. See North Mountain Supply Alcoholmeter.

records.name: O-ring
records.descSnippet: A round ring used as a connector and anchor point where pull comes from any direction.

records.name: oak barrel
records.descSnippet: A charred or toasted oak cask that holds spirit while it matures. The wood adds color, tannin, and flavor and lets a little spirit breathe and oxidize, the traditional home of whiskey, rum, and…

records.name: oak chips
records.descSnippet: Small pieces of oak steeped in spirit to add barrel-like color and flavor quickly, a low-cost alternative to a cask for small batches.

records.name: oil-tanned leather
records.descSnippet: Veg-tan further fed with oils and waxes — supple, pre-dyed, water-resistant and low-maintenance, but harder to tool or carve.

records.name: gombo
records.descSnippet: Green ridged seed pod, mucilaginous when cooked; stewed, fried, or in gumbo.

records.name: oignon
records.descSnippet: Pungent layered bulb, a foundational aromatic; sharp raw, sweet when cooked.

records.name: orange
records.descSnippet: Sweet citrus fruit eaten fresh or juiced; zest and segments flavour both sweet and savoury dishes.

records.name: Origami Dripper
records.descSnippet: The Origami is a fluted dripper that takes both cone and flat-bottom filters, so a single brewer flexes between pour styles. Made in Japan and a modern competition favorite. See Origami Dripper.

records.name: Osborne diamond awl
records.descSnippet: C.S. Osborne diamond awl — the long-established American saddler-tool reference for diamond-awl stitch quality (blade #58 fitted in haft #145).

records.name: Osborne head knife
records.descSnippet: C.S. Osborne's #71 head knife — a long-running American saddler's pattern with a flatter cutting angle, used as a reference for round/head-knife quality.

records.name: papaye
records.descSnippet: Soft tropical fruit with sweet orange flesh and a cavity of black seeds.

records.name: paper filter
records.descSnippet: A bleached paper filter that traps grounds and oils for a clean, sediment-free cup. Shape it to the dripper it serves.

records.name: parrot
records.descSnippet: A small open vessel the spirit runs through on its way to the collection jar, holding a floating hydrometer so the operator can read alcohol strength continuously without stopping the run.

records.name: panais
records.descSnippet: Sweet, nutty cream-coloured taproot; roasted, mashed, or in soups.

records.name: fruit de la passion
records.descSnippet: Wrinkled-skinned tropical fruit with intensely aromatic, tart, seedy pulp.

records.name: petit pois
records.descSnippet: Sweet round green seed from a pod; eaten fresh, frozen, or dried.

records.name: pêche
records.descSnippet: Fuzzy-skinned summer drupe with sweet, juicy flesh around a single stone.

records.name: poire
records.descSnippet: Sweet, soft-fleshed pome fruit; eaten fresh, poached, or baked.

records.name: kaki
records.descSnippet: Glossy orange autumn fruit, honey-sweet when ripe, astringent when not.

records.name: pH meter
records.descSnippet: A meter that reads how acidic or alkaline a wash is. Holding fermentation in the right pH range keeps the yeast healthy and the flavors clean.

records.name: phone sling
records.descSnippet: A small cross-body pouch with a D-ring on a riveted tab and an eyelet-set cord — combines stitching with hardware setting. This is an exemplary template, not a fixed pattern — adapt the pieces,…

records.name: ananas
records.descSnippet: Large tropical fruit with sweet-tart, fibrous yellow flesh and a spiny rind.

records.name: plated column still
records.descSnippet: A column fitted with horizontal plates instead of loose packing. Each plate is a defined stage where vapor bubbles through a shallow pool of liquid, so the operator can count plates and read the…

records.name: prune
records.descSnippet: Juicy drupe in many colours, sweet to tart; eaten fresh, dried (prune), or cooked.

records.name: plunging and pressing
records.descSnippet: End an immersion brew by pressing the plunger down slowly and steadily, separating the grounds from the liquid without churning the bed.

records.name: grenade
records.descSnippet: Leathery-skinned fruit packed with juicy, jewel-like tart-sweet seed arils.

records.name: pomélo
records.descSnippet: The largest citrus, with thick rind and mild, sweet flesh; ancestor of the grapefruit.

records.name: pot still
records.descSnippet: A simple still: a pot that holds the wash, a head, and a condenser. It distills in batches with little reflux, carrying flavor over with the alcohol, so it is the classic choice for whiskey, rum, and…

records.name: pomme de terre
records.descSnippet: Starchy tuber, a global staple; boiled, mashed, roasted, or fried.

records.name: poundboard
records.descSnippet: A dense poly or rubber slab under the work that protects punch and chisel edges and quiets the strike.

records.name: pour-over brew
records.descSnippet: A pour-over brew run: the recipe fixes the method and the ratio, while your beans, grind setting, water, and pour temperature bind when you run it. Every brew is a comparable, citable record.

records.name: pour-over dripper
records.descSnippet: A cone-shaped dripper that holds a paper filter and a bed of grounds while you pour hot water through, brewing one clean cup by gravity. Its angle and ribs shape how fast the water drains.

records.name: pricking and awl stitching
records.descSnippet: Mark the stitch points with a pricking iron, then open each hole with an awl as you sew for maximum control over the angle.

records.name: pricking iron
records.descSnippet: Marks crisp, angled stitch points on the surface; the holes are then opened with an awl as you sew.

records.name: proof and tralle hydrometer
records.descSnippet: A spirit hydrometer carrying both the US proof scale and the Tralle percent-alcohol scale. It reads accurately only on pure water-and-alcohol mixes, so it is used on the clear distillate, not on a…

records.name: proofing water
records.descSnippet: Distilled or de-mineralized water used to proof a spirit down to bottling strength without adding any flavor of its own. Consistent and neutral, it is what a maker reaches for to bring a high-proof…

records.name: puck screen
records.descSnippet: A thin metal mesh placed on top of the puck to spread the water evenly and keep the group head clean.

records.name: pulling an espresso shot
records.descSnippet: Lock in the portafilter and run the pump, watching dose in, yield out, and shot time together. Adjust grind to bring the shot into the target window.

records.name: pulse pouring
records.descSnippet: Add the water in several measured pours rather than one, keeping the bed topped up and the extraction even. Track each pour on the scale.

records.name: citrouille
records.descSnippet: Large winter squash with sweet orange flesh; roasted, in soups, purées and bakes.

records.name: coing
records.descSnippet: Hard, aromatic pome fruit, astringent raw; cooked into pastes, jellies and preserves.

records.name: radis
records.descSnippet: Crisp, peppery root eaten raw; ranges from small red globes to large white daikon.

records.name: Rancilio Silvia
records.descSnippet: Rancilio's Silvia is a single-boiler Italian home machine built with commercial-grade parts, long used as a benchmark for learning espresso. See Rancilio Silvia.

records.name: framboise
records.descSnippet: Soft, hollow red aggregate berry, delicate and tart-sweet.

records.name: groseille
records.descSnippet: Tiny, translucent, very tart red berry borne in strings; used in jellies and garnishes.

records.name: reflux column
records.descSnippet: The vertical column above a still where vapor and returning liquid meet. The taller and better packed it is, the more times that exchange repeats, and the cleaner and stronger the spirit that reaches…

records.name: reflux still
records.descSnippet: A still with a tall packed column above the pot. Rising vapor meets liquid running back down, and that repeated contact strips out flavor and water to give a high, clean strength, the route to vodka…

records.name: refractometer
records.descSnippet: An instrument that reads the dissolved-solids concentration of a brew, so you can calculate extraction and compare cups by number, not just by taste.

records.name: remineralized water
records.descSnippet: Distilled or reverse-osmosis water with a measured mineral blend added back, giving a consistent, repeatable brewing water.

records.name: rhubarbe
records.descSnippet: Tart red-green leaf stalk cooked as a fruit in pies, crumbles and compotes (leaves are toxic).

records.name: Ritza 25 thread
records.descSnippet: Julius Koch's Ritza 25 'Tiger' — a flat, finely braided, lightly waxed polyester thread (0.6-1.7 mm) that is a de-facto hand-stitching standard, widely stocked across North America.

records.name: rivet
records.descSnippet: A two-part metal fastener set through punched holes for permanent, heavy-duty joins and reinforcement.

records.name: rivet setter
records.descSnippet: A matched punch and base that seats and domes a rivet's cap squarely without crushing it.

records.name: laitue romaine
records.descSnippet: Crisp, sturdy lettuce with long upright leaves; the classic Caesar salad green.

records.name: rose petals
records.descSnippet: Aromatic rose petals, a classic charge for steam distillation into rose essential oil and rose water, and an occasional delicate gin botanical.

records.name: rotary cutter
records.descSnippet: A rolling circular blade that tracks straight lines and gentle curves with steady, low-effort control.

records.name: rotary punch
records.descSnippet: A revolving head of graduated tubes that punches clean round holes in several sizes for hardware.

records.name: round knife
records.descSnippet: A full round-bladed saddler's knife that draws long, clean cuts and skives with a rocking motion.

records.name: rutabaga
records.descSnippet: Hardy, sweet-earthy root (turnip x cabbage); mashed, roasted, or in stews.

records.name: rye
records.descSnippet: A grain that ferments to a spicy, peppery spirit. Used on its own or in a mash bill, it gives rye whiskey its characteristic bite.

records.name: saddle soap
records.descSnippet: A mild cleaning and conditioning soap for lifting grime and refreshing leather between treatments.

records.name: saddle stitch
records.descSnippet: The core hand stitch: two needles on one thread cross through each hole in opposite directions, so the seam holds even if a stitch is cut.

records.name: saddle-stitch a seam
records.descSnippet: Join two pieces with a durable hand-sewn seam: mark, punch, stitch, and sear the ends.

records.name: sanding stick
records.descSnippet: Graduated grit on a stick or block to true and smooth glued-up edges before burnishing.

records.name: oignon vert
records.descSnippet: Young onion with a small bulb and long green tops; eaten raw or lightly cooked.

records.name: scrap leather
records.descSnippet: Mixed offcuts sold by weight — the cheapest way to practice cutting, stitching and finishing across many leathers.

records.name: scratch awl
records.descSnippet: A sharp single point for scoring layout lines, tracing patterns onto leather, and general marking.

records.name: seam ripper
records.descSnippet: A hooked point for lifting and cutting stitches to undo a run without nicking the leather.

records.name: searing thread ends
records.descSnippet: Trim the thread tails and melt them flush so a finished saddle stitch can't work loose.

records.name: server
records.descSnippet: A carafe or jug the brewer sits on and the coffee collects in, sized to hold the full brew and pour cleanly into cups.

records.name: set a line of hardware
records.descSnippet: Mark, punch, and set rivets or snaps to fasten layers and attach hardware.

records.name: setting a rivet
records.descSnippet: Punch a hole, seat the rivet's two parts, and dome the cap with a setter and mallet for a permanent join.

records.name: setting a snap
records.descSnippet: Punch the holes and join the four snap parts with a die set so the cap seats centered and clicks cleanly.

records.name: échalote
records.descSnippet: Small, mild, sweet allium bulb; prized in dressings and delicate sauces.

records.name: shotgun condenser
records.descSnippet: A condenser with several narrow inner tubes inside one water jacket, giving far more copper surface and cooling in a shorter body than a single-tube Liebig, useful where output runs fast or space is…

records.name: single-origin coffee
records.descSnippet: Coffee from one origin, farm, or lot, brewed to show the character of that specific place and process rather than a blended profile.

records.name: siphon brewer
records.descSnippet: A vacuum brewer where vapor pressure pushes heated water up into a chamber of grounds, then draws the brew back down through a filter as it cools. Theatrical and very clean.

records.name: skive and fold an edge
records.descSnippet: Thin an edge by skiving, then fold and cement it for a clean, slim turned edge.

records.name: skiving
records.descSnippet: Shave leather thinner where it folds or overlaps so seams and edges stay slim and lie flat.

records.name: skiving knife
records.descSnippet: A flat bevelled blade for thinning leather where it folds or overlaps so seams stay slim.

records.name: snap button
records.descSnippet: A four-part fastener that opens and closes with a press, for flaps, straps and small goods.

records.name: snap hook
records.descSnippet: A spring-gated hook for clipping a strap to a ring — quick to attach and release.

records.name: pois gourmand
records.descSnippet: Plump pea pod eaten whole, crisp and sweet; raw or quickly cooked.

records.name: snap setter
records.descSnippet: A die set that joins the four parts of a snap fastener so the cap seats centered and clean.

records.name: sodium percarbonate
records.descSnippet: An oxygen-releasing cleaner that soaks off organic soils and stains from vessels and tubing, a common no-scrub wash for fermentation gear.

records.name: épinard
records.descSnippet: Tender dark-green leaf eaten raw or wilted; mild, slightly mineral.

records.name: split ring
records.descSnippet: A coiled ring for holding keys and charms onto a fob or strap.

records.name: Starspice Gin Botanicals
records.descSnippet: Starspice supplies gin botanicals including juniper, angelica, and coriander for craft and home distillers. See Starspice.

records.name: steam distillation still
records.descSnippet: A still where steam from a separate source is passed up through a basket of plant material rather than boiling the plants in water. Gentle on heat-sensitive aromatics, it is the workhorse for…

records.name: steel ruler
records.descSnippet: A cork-backed metal rule that measures and guides the knife without the blade shaving its edge.

records.name: steep-and-release brew
records.descSnippet: Immersion plus a clean finish: steep in a valved dripper, then open the valve to release the brew through a paper filter.

records.name: steep-and-release dripper
records.descSnippet: A dripper with a valve in the base: grounds steep like immersion, then you open the valve to release the brew through a paper filter, combining body with a clean finish.

records.name: still cleaner
records.descSnippet: A cleaning preparation made for stills, used to clear scale and residue from the boiler and column so they do not taint the next run.

records.name: Still Spirits Air Still Pro
records.descSnippet: Still Spirits' Air Still Pro is a countertop electric still that can run as a pot or a reflux still, used at home for spirits, essences, and purified water. See Still Spirits Air Still Pro.

records.name: thermometer
records.descSnippet: A probe or dial that reads the temperature of the wash, the vapor at the still head, or the cooling water. Vapor temperature tracks the run's progress and helps the operator judge the cuts.

records.name: StillDragon Bubble Cap Plate
records.descSnippet: StillDragon builds modular copper bubble-cap plates for plated reflux columns, each plate a defined contact stage you can stack to tune purity. A staple of the build-your-own still community. See…

records.name: stitch groover
records.descSnippet: Cuts a shallow channel that recesses the stitch line below the grain so thread sits protected from abrasion.

records.name: stitching awl
records.descSnippet: A diamond-section blade in a haft that pierces each stitch hole at the sewing angle.

records.name: stitching pony
records.descSnippet: A clamp that grips the work upright and frees both hands to run a saddle stitch.

records.name: stovetop kettle
records.descSnippet: A simple kettle heated on the hob. It boils water reliably; you judge brew temperature by timing off the boil rather than a readout.

records.name: strap cutter
records.descSnippet: Sets a fixed width and pulls a long, perfectly parallel strap from a larger piece.

records.name: fraise
records.descSnippet: Sweet red berry eaten fresh, in desserts and preserves; technically an accessory fruit.

records.name: strop
records.descSnippet: A leather strip charged with polishing compound for honing a blade to a final, slicing-sharp finish.

records.name: suede
records.descSnippet: A soft, napped split with a velvety surface; used for linings, backings and lightweight goods rather than structure.

records.name: sunglasses case
records.descSnippet: A folded sleeve with a snap-closed belt loop, glued and stitched along the body — practice in lap seams and setting a snap. This is an exemplary template, not a fixed pattern — adapt the pieces,…

records.name: patate douce
records.descSnippet: Sweet, starchy tuber with orange or purple flesh; roasted, mashed, or fried.

records.name: maïs
records.descSnippet: Sweet kernels on a cob, eaten as a vegetable; boiled, grilled, or cut from the cob.

records.name: swirl and agitation
records.descSnippet: Gently swirl or stir the slurry to settle the grounds and even out the bed. Swirling instead of stabbing keeps the bed flat for a cleaner draw.

records.name: blette
records.descSnippet: Leafy green with edible colourful stalks; both leaf and stem are cooked.

records.name: tamper
records.descSnippet: A weighted disc that compresses the espresso grounds into a level, firm puck so water meets even resistance across the bed.

records.name: tamping
records.descSnippet: Compress the leveled bed into a firm, flat puck with steady, square pressure so the water cannot channel around it.

records.name: tasting and evaluation
records.descSnippet: Taste the brew against its parameters and note aroma, acidity, sweetness, body, and finish. Add a refractometer reading to compare cups by number as well as by palate.

records.name: thermometer
records.descSnippet: A probe or readout for checking water temperature at the pour when the kettle has no readout of its own.

records.name: Third Wave Water
records.descSnippet: Third Wave Water is a mineral packet you add to a gallon of distilled or RO water to hit a target brewing profile, a repeatable way to standardize water. The classic blend is magnesium sulfate,…

records.name: thread zapper
records.descSnippet: A battery hot tip that melts and seals thread tails cleanly, without the soot of an open flame.

records.name: thumper
records.descSnippet: A sealed pot between the still and the condenser, part charged with liquid. Hot vapor bubbling through it re-distills on the fly, raising strength and adding character in one pass, a traditional…

records.name: Timemore Black Mirror
records.descSnippet: The Timemore Black Mirror is an affordable 0.1 gram brewing scale with auto-timer modes, a popular value pick for dialing in pour-over. See Timemore Black Mirror.

records.name: Timemore Chestnut C2
records.descSnippet: The Timemore Chestnut C2 is an affordable hand grinder with 38 mm stainless conical burrs, a common first step up from a blade grinder for filter brewing. See Timemore Chestnut C2.

records.name: toasted oak
records.descSnippet: Oak heated more gently than charring, to a toast that brings out spice, nut, and dried-fruit notes without the heavy smoke of char.

records.name: Tokonole
records.descSnippet: Seiwa's Tokonole — a water-based burnishing gum that is the common reference finish for slick, glassy edges.

records.name: tomate
records.descSnippet: Juicy, savoury-sweet fruit used as a vegetable; raw, cooked, or as sauce.

records.name: turbo yeast
records.descSnippet: Distillers yeast blended with nutrients and buffers to ferment a sugar wash fast and to a high alcohol level. Quick and strong, it leans neutral and dry, so it suits vodka more than a full-bodied…

records.name: navet
records.descSnippet: Mild, slightly peppery root; boiled, roasted or mashed.

records.name: unbleached paper filter
records.descSnippet: A natural, undyed paper filter that works like a bleached one; rinsing before use helps clear any papery taste.

records.name: utility knife
records.descSnippet: An inexpensive replaceable-blade knife that handles most straight cuts on thin to medium leather.

records.name: V60 pour-over brew
records.descSnippet: A single-cup cone pour-over: dose and grind, heat the water to the roast, bloom, then build the brew in pulses with a gentle swirl, and taste the result.

records.name: variable-temperature kettle
records.descSnippet: An electric kettle that heats water to a set target and holds it there, so you can match the water to the roast and repeat it every brew.

records.name: vegetable-tanned leather
records.descSnippet: Hide tanned with plant tannins: firm, carves and tools well, and the natural choice for structural work and wet-molding. Patinas with use.

records.name: Vengeance Stills Copper Proofing Parrot
records.descSnippet: Vengeance Stills' copper proofing parrot holds a hydrometer in the running stream so the operator can read strength continuously through the spirit run. See Vengeance Stills Copper Proofing Parrot.

records.name: VST LAB Coffee III
records.descSnippet: The VST LAB Coffee III is a US-made digital refractometer long used as the lab reference for measuring brew strength and calculating extraction. See VST LAB Coffee III.

records.name: refractometer
records.descSnippet: An instrument that reads sugar content from how much a drop of liquid bends light, letting a brewer or distiller check a wash's starting gravity from a few drops rather than a full sample.

records.name: water filter pitcher
records.descSnippet: A jug that filters tap water through a cartridge to reduce chlorine and hardness before brewing, a simple first step toward better-tasting water.

records.name: water preparation
records.descSnippet: Treat the water before brewing: filter the tap, or remineralize a distilled base to a target recipe, so mineral content stays consistent cup to cup.

records.name: water temperature selection
records.descSnippet: Match water temperature to the roast: hotter for light roasts, cooler for dark, so extraction lands in balance. Record the temperature you actually pour at.

records.name: cresson
records.descSnippet: Peppery aquatic leaf; eaten raw in salads and sandwiches or in soups.

records.name: pastèque
records.descSnippet: Large melon with crisp, watery, sweet red flesh and a hard green rind.

records.name: waxed linen thread
records.descSnippet: Traditional waxed natural-fiber thread with a matte look favored for classic and repairable work.

records.name: waxed polyester thread
records.descSnippet: Braided, lightly waxed polyester — strong, UV-stable and forgiving; the everyday default for hand saddle stitching.

records.name: WDT tool
records.descSnippet: A cluster of fine needles stirred through the dry espresso grounds to break up clumps and even the bed before tamping, for a more uniform extraction.

records.name: wet molding
records.descSnippet: Dampen veg-tan and shape it over a form; as it dries it sets and holds the molded shape.

records.name: wheat
records.descSnippet: A soft grain that ferments to a gentle, mellow spirit. It rounds out a whiskey mash bill and is the base of wheat vodka.

records.name: whetstone
records.descSnippet: A graded abrasive stone for grinding and refining a keen edge on knives and bevelers — a sharp tool is a safe tool.

records.name: whole bean coffee
records.descSnippet: Roasted coffee in whole-bean form, ground fresh just before brewing for the best aroma and a grind matched to the method.

records.name: wine yeast
records.descSnippet: A yeast bred for fruit and grape musts, tolerant of higher alcohol and chosen to preserve fruit aromatics. It ferments the wash behind brandy and fruit spirits.

records.name: wing divider
records.descSnippet: A two-leg compass that scribes a stitching line a fixed distance in from the edge, and steps off even spacing.

records.name: worm condenser
records.descSnippet: A coiled tube, the worm, submerged in a tub of cold water. Vapor winding through the coil gives up its heat slowly, the oldest condenser form and still valued for the heavier, fuller spirit it tends…

records.name: zipper
records.descSnippet: A toothed closure stitched into bags and cases; setting it cleanly calls for a few dedicated tools.

records.name: courgette
records.descSnippet: Tender summer squash eaten skin and all; sautéed, grilled, or raw.
